newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin-Clinton summit to be put off for a day.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin-Clinton summit to be put off for a day.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin and Bill Clinton have agreed to put off their planned March 19 summit in Helsinki for a day to allow Clinton more time to recover from the knee surgery he underwent on Friday, the Kremlin said.

"According to a mutual agreement reached by Russian President Boris Yelstin and U.S. President Bill Clinton the meeting planned for March 19, 1997 in Helsinki is postponed for one day," a Kremlin statement said.

The two leaders originally agreed to hold their two-day summit in Finland, which neighbours Russia, instead of the United States where it had been due because of heart problems suffered by Yeltsin in the past eight months.
But a fall by Clinton early on Friday morning in Florida meant that it was the American leader's health rather than Yeltsin's which ended up casting doubt over the summit plans.

A U.S. official said in Washington on Sunday that the previously announced summit schedule would remain essentially the same. Clinton would leave Washington late on March 19 and arrive in Helsinki midday Thursday.
The Kremlin statement did not detail Yeltsin's revised travel plans.
